title: Root cubes and two-vertex deletions from daisy grids
summary: Daisy cubes are finite partial cubes that admit an isometric hypercube embedding whose labels form a Boolean down-set. Call a vertex a root if it can receive the all-zero label in such an embedding. Using the peripheral $Θ$-class characterization implicit in earlier work of Taranenko and of Xie--Xu, and Vesel's description of possible zero vertices, we prove the following intrinsic refinement. If exactly $b$ classes are peripheral on both sides, then $G\cong G_0\square Q_b$, where $G_0$ has a unique root and the roots of $G$ induce the displayed convex $b$-cube.
